author: apersoma
body:
Modifier that turns the game into a turnbased team strategy game + deputy.
Reveals all win conditions at the start of the game.
Defense inherent to roles are disabled.
Nomination phase is skipped.
If no players are killed for 5 nights the game ends in a draw.
If no players can be killed the game ends in a draw. (this is on the safe side, will not draw a game where players can die but might fail to draw a game where players can't die.)
Players can opt for a tie. If all living players are opting for a tie, the game ends in a draw.
A few roles are modified while active: 
- Jester: Wants to die (not necessarily be executed), and can kill anyone when dead.

author: renechcdda
body:
#### Summary
Bugfixes "'None'-skill crafting counts as max level, not level 0"

#### Purpose of change
We have a variety of crafting tasks which are so trivial that they should not even be assigned a skill, because even with a difficulty of 0 they can level that skill up to 1.

Unfortunately since they have no skill assigned, the character could never have levels in the (non-existent) skill, which meant that crafting these recipes always counted as if the skill level was 0.

Related to #65433 though I couldn't think of a way to accomplish this at the time.

#### Describe the solution
If there is no skill defined, count our skill level as if it was MAX_SKILL (10).

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
These recipes can still have fail chance due to encumbrance, limb scores, etc. Perhaps they should not be able to fail even in those circumstances?

#### Testing
All images with default 8/8/8/8 character with all skills at maximum, no proficiencies other than default ones.

Before:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26727224-bfb0-4ebf-8b66-52c80b0494d2)

After:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4d2ebdb-8da8-4d6f-804d-8c18a440b824)

This pull request includes several changes to the codebase to refactor how links are generated and to improve the structure and reusability of HTML templates. The most important changes include the consolidation of link generation logic, the introduction of a base HTML template, and the reorganization of configuration imports.

Improvements to link generation:

* [`server/database/models.py`](diffhunk://#diff-d0fca013b75e944909527a42ef2cd323401ec27f146beefc1353d4412f38b58fL218-R245): Simplified the link generation logic by consolidating multiple link types into a single structure and using helper functions to generate links.
* [`server/ogc_apis/features/implementation/pre_render_helper.py`](diffhunk://#diff-34d86e5a644eb207b80f46cdbd00392b6cb985f021109fcb4c704147b4673ac9L1-R29): Refactored the link generation functions to support multiple formats and ensure consistent link creation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-34d86e5a644eb207b80f46cdbd00392b6cb985f021109fcb4c704147b4673ac9L1-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-34d86e5a644eb207b80f46cdbd00392b6cb985f021109fcb4c704147b4673ac9L36-R77)

Enhancements to HTML templates:

* [`server/jinja_templates/basic.html`](diffhunk://#diff-9807dc7e2929a962dbf543ef7ec5f001810c38e9b53a21ea03c7900bb6b11f72R1-R36): Introduced a base HTML template to standardize the structure of HTML pages.
* `server/jinja_templates/collection.html`, `server/jinja_templates/conformance_declaration.html`, `server/jinja_templates/landing_page.html`: Updated templates to extend from the new base template, improving consistency and maintainability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dc4fb1fa0c181f628f30d10427778e5e82c04066906c02f274fe89ddbc23cc2aL1-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1ba2521f681c8ef8cc6242c7da529b525c85afb47253ca3163d1070af1e45818R1-R17) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a61cc5ae7623441ac2be202c0acea68d080e93bd49b09eb1b618a8ce3874ff48R1-R12)

Reorganization of configuration imports:

* `server/ogc_apis/__init__.py`, `server/ogc_apis/config/__init__.py`, `server/ogc_apis/config/formats.py`, `server/ogc_apis/config/params.py`, `server/ogc_apis/config/paths.py`, `server/ogc_apis/config/templates.py`: Reorganized configuration imports to improve modularity and clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-841dbd4b141520cdd2b49542decf1be9184dac30818de53dec6a4e7137fb7ae5R1-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a36cd03639eeaca41840f2f22e83a1ca4637994b6f700189d49db0104f03caf4R1-R3) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-62765db2d45311ae5bbcaeb85f422eeb7b83c423ac706d087bcd7124ecff830dR1-R30) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cdfba99b4db6dfc5c2fa07e24c7848edcd14619dab7d4df4dd393e559bb4f0fcR1-R14) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-784af08aef36f1deb1a8585f93fbc65d2f203616153f5f709f3c05ce7bec72c5R1-R2) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-272a1bde855564f043dc3b4b5f1028bddc016cee94b6ee2b81f40053a060f8f9R1-R19)

## What are the changes the user will see?
Potentially faster loading and/or improved performance.

## Why am I making these changes?
https://thelinuxcode.com/mastering-javascript-maps-an-expert-guide/

## What are the changes from a developer perspective?
- The definition of `allMoves` was changed from an object to a `Map` in `src/data/data-lists.ts`.
- All uses of `allMoves[...]` were replaced with `allMoves.get(...)`.
- `Object.values(allMoves)` replaced with `allMoves.values()`.
- `allMoves[move.id] = move` replaced with `allMoves.set(move.id, move)` in `src/data/init-moves.ts`.
- `loadMoveAnimAssets()` in `src/utils/move-anim-utils.ts` simplified.

author: arms2025
body:
We are researchers and analyzed the test doubles (mocks) in the test code of the project. In our analysis of the project, we observed that

+ The `get` method, which is previously stubbed, is executed with the argument "sonar.branch.target", but this specific argument is not stubbed, resulting in a mismatch stubbing. This mismatch occurs in the test `BranchParamsValidatorImplTest.validate_lagacy_and_branch_name`.
+ The `get` method, which is previously stubbed, is executed with the argument "sonar.branch.name", but this specific argument is not stubbed, resulting in a mismatch stubbing. This mismatch occurs in the test `BranchParamsValidatorImplTest.validate_lagacy_and_target_name`. 

In this pull request, we propose a solution to resolve the mismatch stubbings.

Mismatched stubbing occurs when a mocked method is stubbed with specific arguments in a test but later invoked with different arguments in the code, potentially causing unexpected behavior. Mockito recommends addressing these issues, (https://www.javadoc.io/doc/org.mockito/mockito-core/latest/org/mockito/exceptions/misusing/PotentialStubbingProblem.html)

<!-- If you are new to the Delta-V repository, please read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/DeltaV-Station/Delta-v/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) -->

## About the PR
The actual Kitsune PR! Finally playable after a year and a half of the idea being worked on. Kitsune are a race of shapeshifters that can turn into foxes, and have a stronger then average connection to the noosphere that manifests in a small amount of control over fire. (redid because the title got messed up because my computer is dumb)

## Why / Balance
Kitsune are an idea that's been around for... a while. This finally brings them to life, and in a way that creates a species that actually interacts and leans further into Delta-V's unique content. Balancewise, they take a reduced amount of heat and cold in exchange for an increased amount of blunt damage, and 50% more poison damage (due to a naturally weaker constitution), and in their fox form they lose their resistances and gain a weakness to slashing and pierce as well in exchange for more speed. They also naturally have the lightweight drunk trait. On the pros side, they deal heat damage with their unarmed attacks, and have a natural psionic bonus chance, along with the ability to summon up a small, cool, wisp of flame to light up the dark. Finally, they actually have an interaction with holy damage, taking a reduced amount of it to represent that they have a foot in both sides of the veil. Hopefully planning to expand on that in the future when psionics are expanded.

Balance on the fox form side, as mentioned they have higher speed, and they don't drop their inventory like some polymorphs have done in the past, but in exchange they are forced to revert back when stunned, crit, or dead. This means it's actually possible to arrest them without having to crit them, for one. It also means that nothing is lost forever just because a kitsune might not want to transform back. 

## Technical details
So, aside from a couple of files, this touches as little upstream code as possible. It does have some code taken from the Geras port on impstation relating to changing a polymorph's color based on the original form, so credit there. Otherwise, a ton of credit to Sol for their work on the C#, this PR probably would have taken another 6 months without their help.

I noticed a possible regression while upgrading to 3.11 in https://github.com/jippi/dottie/pull/217 - this behavior was not present in 3.10 which i upgraded from

The expansion of `[${UNSET:-${BAR-defaultValue}}]` used to result in `[]` but now result in `[defaultValue]`

In zsh/bash running these echo's give the following output, which I think Expand should match

```
$ BAR=""; echo "[${UNSET:-${BAR-defaultValue}}]"
[]

$ BAR="set"; echo "[${UNSET:-${BAR-defaultValue}}]"
[set]
```

## NOTE

This is not a fix, but a reproducible test case to show-case the issue

author: deploy-demon[bot]
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [ghcr.io/navidrome/navidrome](https://redirect.github.com/navidrome/navidrome) | minor | `0.54.5` -> `0.55.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>navidrome/navidrome (ghcr.io/navidrome/navidrome)</summary>

### [`v0.55.0`](https://redirect.github.com/navidrome/navidrome/releases/tag/v0.55.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/navidrome/navidrome/compare/v0.54.5...v0.55.0)

#### Navidrome 0.55.0 - Big Refactor (BFR) Release Notes

##### Overview

Navidrome 0.55.0 introduces the highly anticipated Big Refactor (BFR), significantly enhancing core functionalities,
and introducing robust new features. This release brings substantial improvements in handling file management and
metadata usage and customization.

##### New Features

-   **Multiple Artists in Albums and Songs**: Navidrome now supports albums and tracks with multiple artists, allowing
    users to group tracks with different artists under a single album. This feature enhances the organization of
    compilation albums and multi-artist collaborations.

-   **Contributors and Performers**: Composer, conductor, and other contributors can now be added to tracks, providing
    detailed information about the creators and performers involved in the music production process.

-   **Album Versions**: Support for `ALBUMVERSION` tag has been added, enabling users to differentiate between standard
    releases, deluxe editions, remasters, and other versions of the same album. This feature enhances album categorization
    and provides a more comprehensive music library experience.

-   **Multi-valued Tags**: Support for multi-valued tags has been improved, allowing users to store multiple values for
    any single tag. This feature enhances metadata flexibility and enables more detailed categorization.

-   **Custom Tags**: Support for user-defined custom tags has been added, allowing enhanced metadata flexibility and
    personalized categorization. [Learn more](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/customtags/).

-   **Smart Playlists Enhancements**: Smart Playlists supports all newly added tags, including multiple artists,
    contributors, performers, and album versions, as well as custom tags. It also behaves better with multi-valued tags.
    [Learn more](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/smartplaylists/).

-   **Persistent IDs**: Tracks and albums now use persistent IDs (PIDs), ensuring stability in playlists, favorites,
    and external integrations, even if your files move or are renamed. PIDs can also be configured to change the way
    Navidrome disambiguates albums and tracks. It is now also possible to group albums by folder,
    bay setting `PID.Album="folder"`. [Learn more](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/pids/).

-   **Scanner Improvements**: Optimized file scanning, with improved handling of file moves and retagging, "watcher" mode
    for real-time updates, resumable scans and enhanced performance during library updates.

-   **Improved Handling of Missing Files**: Enhanced mechanisms for managing missing files ensure better accuracy and
    easier troubleshooting. [Learn more](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/missing-files/).

-   **Beginner-Friendly Tagging Guidelines**: A comprehensive tagging guide has been introduced to assist new users in
    properly tagging their music collections. [Learn more](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/tagging-guidelines/).

##### New configuration options

-   `PID.Album`
-   `PID.Track`
-   `Scanner.Enabled`
-   `Scanner.Schedule`
-   `Scanner.WatcherWait`
-   `Scanner.ScanOnStartup`
-   `Subsonic.AppendSubtitle`
-   `Subsonic.ArtistParticipations`
-   `Subsonic.DefaultReportRealPath`
-   `Subsonic.LegacyClients`
-   `Tags`

##### Deprecated/Changed configuration options:

-   `ScanSchedule` was renamed to `Scanner.Schedule`
-   `Scanner.Extractor` was removed. `ffmpeg` extractor is not supported anymore and Navidrome will now always use TagLib for metadata extraction.
-   `Scanner.GenreSeparators` was removed. Use `Tags.genre.Split` instead. Check the [Custom Tags][custom-tags] documentation for more information.
-   `Scanner.GroupAlbumReleases` was removed. Use `PID.Album` instead.

Check the [Configuration Options](https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/configuration-options/) documentation for
more information.

##### Breaking Changes

-   Artist favourites and artist ratings will be lost after the upgrade.
-   Albums may move around (change grouping), as the default disambiguation logic is slightly different than the previous version. If you want to keep the same behaviour as before, add this line to your configuration *before* upgrading:

```toml
PID.Album = "album_legacy"
```

or as env var

```shell
ND_PID_ALBUM=album_legacy
```

##### Upgrade Instructions

1.  **Backup Database**: Before upgrading, create a backup of your current Navidrome database.
2.  **Stop Navidrome**: Ensure Navidrome is not running before proceeding.
3.  **Replace Binary**: Download and replace the existing Navidrome binary with the latest version (0.55.0).
    If using docker, pull the `latest` image.
4.  **Start Navidrome**: Restart Navidrome to automatically migrate the database schema. The upgrade process
    will trigger a full scan of your library, which may take some time depending on the size of your collection. While
    this full scan is in progress, please avoid using Navidrome, as the data will be unstable until the process finishes.

author: zakariathr22
body:
## Description  
Wrapped the `StackPanel` inside a `Border` in the **Settings** page to fix a slight blurriness issue when the main window is maximized.  

## Motivation and Context  
- This change improves the visual clarity of items inside the `StackPanel`.
- This was a subtle and hard-to-notice side effect caused by #1791.
- It seems that modifying the visual properties of a `StackPanel` inside a `ScrollView` or `ScrollViewer` can cause rendering issues when the window is maximized.
- Wrapping the StackPanel inside a Border or Grid can help stabilize the rendering.

## How Has This Been Tested?  
- Manually tested by maximizing and resizing the window to check for blurriness.  

## Screenshots (if appropriate):  
The difference is subtle and not easily captured in screenshots. The blurriness requires deep observation while maximizing the window to notice it.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)  
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

body:
libsqlite is really slow building, and causes the MINIMAL build step to be much slower (especially since it's not parallel). 
The testers that use frozen caches also do not depend on it, as they use the ALL library target.
This has the effect that it pushes building this library from the fast/highly parallel build-linux builder to the test builders, and makes build-linux faster.

author: joshcooper
body:
This is the same as https://github.com/puppetlabs/puppetlabs-puppet_agent/pull/757 but for apt.

Updates the `puppet_agent::install_task` so it's possible to install deb-based packages from https://apt-puppetcore.puppet.com (debian and ubuntu). Credentials are required when installing from apt-puppetcore. The username defaults to `forge-key` and the password must be set to your forge API token.

```
❯ /opt/puppetlabs/bolt/bin/bolt task run puppet_agent::install collection=puppetcore8 version=8.11.0 password=${PUPPET_FORGE_TOKEN} --targets ...
..
  23:25:51 +0000 INFO: Downloading https://apt-puppetcore.puppet.com/public/puppet8-release-jammy.deb
...
  Setting up puppet-agent (8.11.0-1jammy) ...
```

Also updates the `puppet_agent` class so it's possible to manage agent  versions over time:

```puppet
class { 'puppet_agent':
  package_version => '8.11.0',
  collection => 'puppetcore8',
  password => Sensitive(...)
}
```

And it updates the Dockerfiles used to test install and upgrades. See docker/README.md for details.

I haven't changed the default behavior of the module if the collection is unspecified or is one of the existing puppet7, puppet7-nightly, puppet8, etc collections. If no collection is specified, then it continues to use the "unversioned" release package from `apt.puppet.com`.

author: dotnomad
body:
This PR adds a new GitHub workflow and associated actions to release, version, and list Connect extensions.

#### High Level

To facilitate this I'll go over some of the high level changes:
- Extensions that we TAR now have a new `extension` section in the `manifest.json` that stores metadata that fills the extension list
  - This includes a `name`, `title`, `description`, `homepage` (the link to the GitHub page for the extension currently), and a [semver](https://semver.org/) `version`
- A new base level file called `extensions.json`
  - This currently just contains `{ extensions: [] }` but is where the gallery's Extension List will live
  - This file is not intended to be edited by hand except for removal (documentation on this to come)
- A new `scripts` folder that contains a `extension.list.ts` script that uses GitHub releases created by the new workflow to add to the Extension List
  - This is a TypeScript file so there are additional files to add TypeScript support and types for easier script writing

#### GitHub Workflow

There are 3 new GitHub actions in this PR:
- `lint-extension`: to check if a given extension name in the repo contains the new `extension` section in its `manifest.json` and that the `version` string is a valid semver
- `package-extension`: to TAR up the extension for releases
  - Takes an extension name and optionally an `artifact-name` for custom workflow extensions (see more below)
- `release-extension`: to release the packaged extension as a GitHub Release and update the Extension List with the data of the release for the Gallery to utilize

The main workflow - `extensions.yml` checks for changes to extensions to lint, package, and if on `main` release the extensions.

It does this in two groups:
- `simple-extensions`: includes all extensions in directories that can just be tarball-ed to release
- `complex-extensions`: all extensions that require custom workflows
  - The only one in this group is `publisher-command-center` at the moment
  
Once all of the extensions have been released as GitHub Releases the extension list script is run to capture that information for the Gallery to consume in something like the below:

<details>
  <summary>Example `extensions.json`</summary>
  
  ```json
  {
  "extensions": [
    {
      "name": "publisher-command-center",
      "title": "Publisher Command Center",
      "description": "A dashboard for publishers to help manage and track their content",
      "homepage": "https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-extensions/tree/main/extensions/publisher-command-center",
      "latestVersion": {
        "version": "2.0.2",
        "released": "2025-03-11T22:55:27Z",
        "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/publisher-command-center%40v2.0.2/publisher-command-center.tar.gz"
      },
      "versions": [
        {
          "version": "2.0.2",
          "released": "2025-03-11T22:55:27Z",
          "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/publisher-command-center%40v2.0.2/publisher-command-center.tar.gz"
        },
        {
          "version": "2.0.1",
          "released": "2025-03-11T22:39:02Z",
          "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/publisher-command-center%40v2.0.1/publisher-command-center.tar.gz"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "reaper",
      "title": "Reaper",
      "description": "A view to a kill.",
      "homepage": "https://github.com/posit-dev/connect-extensions/tree/main/extensions/reaper",
      "latestVersion": {
        "version": "2.0.4",
        "released": "2025-03-11T22:54:56Z",
        "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/reaper%40v2.0.4/reaper.tar.gz"
      },
      "versions": [
        {
          "version": "2.0.4",
          "released": "2025-03-11T22:54:56Z",
          "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/reaper%40v2.0.4/reaper.tar.gz"
        },
        {
          "version": "2.0.3",
          "released": "2025-03-11T22:42:29Z",
          "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/reaper%40v2.0.3/reaper.tar.gz"
        },
        {
          "version": "2.0.1",
          "released": "2025-03-11T22:38:48Z",
          "url": "https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/releases/download/reaper%40v2.0.1/reaper.tar.gz"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  ```
</details> 

The actions and general `extensions.yml` workflow files are heavily commented to explain the steps and some of the decisions made.
  
##### Custom Workflow Extensions

The "Complex Extensions" have custom workflows. They cannot simply be packaged and require some additional steps to package, and other steps potentially in the future.

The one example now is `publisher-command-center` which needs to setup `node` to do a `build` of the frontend it ships. This cannot be handled generically so requires a more custom built GitHub workflow to be utilized by the main workflow - `extensions.yml`.

The custom workflows can use the same actions above (and in this PR do) for easy linting, packaging, and releasing.

#### Approach

There were a few goals I kept in mind when writing the workflows and script:
- Simple extensions should have little to no edits in GitHub Workflows to work
  - With this PR only 1 line is required to add a new extension
- Don't release every extension in every directory to avoid releasing an extension earlier than developers of it would like
- Complex extensions like `publisher-command-center` should be possible to build and release
- Actions in the workflow should be generalized to avoid duplicate code
- The flow should be easily extendable
- The flow should run in parallel wherever possible
- It should be easy to consume the latest version of an extension and versions in the Extension List should be sorted to help this as well
- Commit once to update the extension list
- Pull Requests should see if an extension would release, and with what TAR (included as artifact(s) of the workflow)

#### Workflow testing

Each step was done as a POC and then generalized to Actions and then other extensions. The development for this was done on a fork [`dotNomad/connect-extensions`](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions) to run the workflows.

There are a few workflows I'll point out that were done as tests:
- [Workflow #77](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799577805/job/38599029749) updates two extensions, one with an error one without. The success still updates the extension list and the failure does not get released
- [Workflow #78](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799601555) updates two extensions at once successfully
- [Workflow #80](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799629758) shows no extensions updating and no extension commands run around linting, packaging, etc.
- [Workflow #81](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799648074) shows an update to a single extension
- [Workflow #82](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799692825/job/38599376279) shows a correct linting failure
- Workflows [#83](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799794597/job/38599706942) and [#84](https://github.com/dotNomad/connect-extensions/actions/runs/13799796428/job/38599723775) show two workflows completing near-the-same-time and the extension list still updating.

body:
### WHY

Normally a system is dedicated to call the Cinemachine brailn `ManualUpdate()` to update its usage of virtual cameras.

When the camera entity has a `CameraLookAtIntent` that system was avoiding the Cinemachine update, so when a scene used `movePlayerTo()` with the `cameraTarget` parameter, combined with the SDK `VirtualCamera` usage, the Cinemachine behaviour broke without repair because it didn't get updated.

### WHAT

Fixed cinemachine not getting updated while `CameraLookAtIntent` component is on the camera entity.

### TEST INSTRUCTIONS

1. Download the build from this PR
2. **Confirm that all the "in-world camera" functionalities work correctly**
3. Confirm the test steps from this recently-merged PR are still OK: https://github.com/decentraland/unity-explorer/pull/3473
4. Go to genesis city, to the Mine Sweeper minigame at `-30,3` and confirm that if you move the camera before entering the game, the camera gets overridden correctly when the game starts, pointing at the game. Exit and enter the game several times to confirm the camera doesn't get locked with the state before starting the game.

body:
Your general must be the character with the highest leadership in your army. I have added a check to determine what the highest leadership of the characters in your army is (excluding characters who can't be generals like Loners), and then confirm that the selected general has that leadership.

![GeneralLeadershipValidation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27236593-4254-485e-a8c6-5fb9c6c3e1b2)

There are, of course, a few edge cases where a general must be a certain type of character even if they aren't the highest leadership. For example a Vampire Counts army's general must be a wizard, so if you have a Vampire Count without the Wizard option (Ld 8) and a Necromancer Acolyte (Ld 7), the Necromancer must be the general despite not having the highest leadership. Currently this check does not validate for this. Perhaps if there was a way of tweaking validation errors based on the selected army, this could be done fairly cleanly?

body:
### What does this PR do?
* Fixed `_build_bank_hier()` function to build a proper hierarchy.
* Fixed `list_()` function to support both types of sets.

### What issues does this PR fix or reference?
Incorrect minion data hierarchy.
Incorrect minion list retrieval.
### Previous Behavior
* When minion data is stored, plugin would add `"."` to `{bank_prefix}{separator}minions` set, instead of `minion_id`.
* `{bank_prefix}{separator}minions/{minion_id}` set is created and `"."` added to it.
* `list_()` function, which is used to fetch the list of minion_ids from cache in `manage.*` runners, would target `{bank_keys_prefix}{separator}minions` set instead of `{bank_prefix}{separator}minions`, returning an empty list.

### New Behavior
* `minion_id` is added to `{bank_prefix}{separator}minions` set.
* `{bank_prefix}{separator}minions/{minion_id}` is not created.
* `list_()` function targets `{bank_prefix}{separator}{bank}` first and if empty list is returned, `{bank_keys_prefix}{separator}{bank}`.

body:
Checkpoints:
- 33-channel (old): https://huggingface.co/hunyuanvideo-community/HunyuanVideo-I2V-33ch
- 16-channel (new): https://huggingface.co/hunyuanvideo-community/HunyuanVideo-I2V

Code:

```python
import torch
from diffusers import HunyuanVideoImageToVideoPipeline, HunyuanVideoTransformer3DModel
from diffusers.utils import load_image, export_to_video

# Available checkpoints: "hunyuanvideo-community/HunyuanVideo-I2V" and "hunyuanvideo-community/HunyuanVideo-I2V-33ch"
model_id = "hunyuanvideo-community/HunyuanVideo-I2V"
transformer = HunyuanVideoTransformer3DModel.from_pretrained(
    model_id, subfolder="transformer", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
)
pipe = HunyuanVideoImageToVideoPipeline.from_pretrained(
    model_id, transformer=transformer, torch_dtype=torch.float16
)
pipe.vae.enable_tiling()
pipe.to("cuda")

prompt = "A man with short gray hair plays a red electric guitar."
image = load_image(
    "https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/diffusers/guitar-man.png"
)

output = pipe(image=image, prompt=prompt).frames[0]
export_to_video(output, "output.mp4", fps=15)
```

author: ckreibich
body:
Alright, I have no idea how "correct" any of this is for PHP's Cake framework, but:
* URLs with garbage after the package & tag views get redirected back to "clean" URLs
* We now correctly render README paths to Github — you can try [here](https://packages.zeek.org/packages/view/1c43296f-78de-11ec-ba82-0a598146b5c6).
* We strip links in READMEs when they're not from Github, just keeping their anchor text

This last part ignores #6 for the time being but should work correctly if and when those READMEs appear.

This is actually running now on packages.zeek.org, hopefully improving the disk-fill situation. :crossed_fingers: 

The site has a lot of problems — the whole PHP dependency thing is busted on the instance we're running the site on. The `composer` version installed is old and uses ridiculous amounts of memory during dependency resolution, while a newer version avoids that but then blows up in the actual package dependencies because we're installing one package from a version called "dev-master", which has moved on and no longer works with our Cake version. I tried a couple of things but couldn't figure it out (interestingly, this dependency management behaves almost like zkg's but fails when it would be damn handy to be able to specify a git commit has as version — hah!).

I've simply preserved the `vendor/` tree in the resulting installation, which seems to work since we're not changing anything at that level.

Really good motivation to get the new version of the site up and running!

Resolves #8.

author: pglob
body: - There was a bug where you could send a status notification when booting up to fault the charger. Then clear the fault to skip the boot process and go into an available state. - Also prevent going offline when booting up. - Also add a few more test cases for our MessageController. - Additionally, the "Go offline" and "Simulate exceptions" buttons are now hidden when booting up. The reasoning behind these changes is that since we are not in an OCPP state yet, the handling for being offline or faulting is undefined. I think this was the easiest solution too.

author: jaredstanbrook
body:
## Overview:

This PR enhances the development environment setup by configuring essential tools and extensions to ensure consistent formatting and linting across the project. Specifically, we’ve focused on:

- Formatting (Prettier): Automatically formats most files on save.
- Python:
    - Type Checking with Pylance.
    - Code Formatting with autopep8.
- JavaScript:
    - Linting with EsLint.
    - Code Formatting with EsLint.
- Django HTML: Linting with djlint.

## How It Works:

- Prettier: Automatically formats most files upon saving.
- Python: The autopep8 extension formats Python files, while Pylance handles type checking.
- JavaScript: EsLint is used for both linting and formatting.
- Django HTML: djlint ensures proper formatting and linting for Django HTML templates.

## Pre-Commit Hook Setup:

The following pre-commit hooks are configured to run checks and ensure code quality before committing:

1. General Code Quality:
    - Check case conflicts, trailing whitespace, and end-of-file issues.
    - Ensure proper formatting for YAML, JSON, and TOML files.
    - Reject commits that add large files or merge conflicts.
    - Prevent committing to main or master branches.

2. Python:
    - autopep8: Automatically formats Python files to adhere to PEP 8 standards.

3. Django:
    - djlint: Reformats Django HTML templates.

4. JavaScript:
    - EsLint: Lints and formats JavaScript files.

## Handling Hook Failures:

**If any pre-commit hook fails, it will provide feedback on the error, directing you to the issue. You will need to fix the error or the hook will automatically fix the error, then you must stage the fix, and re-commit**

These hooks help ensure that all code adheres to our formatting and linting standards, improving consistency and quality across the project.

Following feedback from player "Precellence" about the redundancy of the [22] Stunning Bounty, we've decided to remove it from the sandbox. The Stunning Bounty was made as an upgrade to the Purging Shock Rifle, but ultimately the idea didn't come out of a necessity, and instead was just an experiment to see if an upgraded Purging Shock Rifle could be made.

The weapon proved to be too bad of an investment for a REQ tier 8, and we couldn't drop it lower due to the other Shock Rifle variants needing to stay in their REQ tiers up to 7.

## Valkyrie tier and ammo increase

Following feedback from player "Precellence" about the low ammo count of the [13] Valkyrie, we've agreed with his comments and increased the weapon's ammo count from 10 to 16 total shots, while also bringing the weapon from REQ tier 7 to 8.

As the Valkyrie is a recreation of the Nornfang sniper from Halo 5 which had 16 shots, this change was natural, and helps align player expectations of the weapon with how they were in Halo 5. The REQ tier increase to 8 was necessary due to the high impact of the extra 6 shots.

## Phantom Assassin ammo increase

Following feedback from player "Precellence" about the low ammo count of the [26] Phantom Assassin, we've decided to increase it from 4 to 6 total shots. As the weapon uses aim-tracked rockets, they can often be more difficult to hit on moving targets, where the M41 Tracker will still be more useful, even with just 4 total shots, and in the same REQ tier.

## Sentry Off Writh 'Kul camo addition

Following feedback from player "Precellence" about the [34] Sentry Off Writh 'Kul needing some special effect to stay on par with the [30] Doom Off Reach, we've taken his suggestions and added two camo traits to the weapon.

The first camo trait is a constant 70% invisibility while holding the weapon, with a slow decay time. The second camo trait can be activated by zooming with the weapon, and nearly instantly turns the player to 100% invisibility. Shooting while zoomed takes the player out of camo, but the camo returns quickly after the shooting is stopped.

We believe this camo trait is a unique option for a handheld turret at REQ tier 7 to the Doom Off Reach, which is all about rushing near the enemy with a high damage resistance.

## Power Off Jega Rdomnai sprint speed increase

Following feedback from player "Precellence" about the [36] Power Off Jega Rdomnai needing some upgrade to be worthy as a REQ tier 7, we've added a slight sprint speed increase to the weapon.

One big aspect of the weapon is full camo while walking, but it's countered by the loud infected sound emitted from the Infected Energy Sword base weapon. We did not want to compromise on the design choices that make this weapon unique in that regard, so we opted for increasing the sprint speed instead.

The sprint speed increase is currently identical to the speed increase gained from the "Upgraded Sprinting" ability boost.

## Knight Off Zeretus ammo increase

Following feedback from player "Precellence" about the slightly lower than ideal ammo count of the [39] Knight Off Zeretus, we've increased its total shot count from 6 to 8. We want to give players the ability to not worry about the ammo usage of this weapon too much, as getting kills with it is not always consistent.

## Broken Installation overhaul

We saw the [44] Broken Installation as an outlier in REQ tier 5 in comparison to its counterparts: the [12] Valor Off Dinh and Convergence Bulldog. The weapon performed too good at long range, while also holding 30 total shots, which allowed around 20 average kills for the weapon.

We've changed the weapon's projectile count from 3 to 2, and decreased the total ammo from 30 to 20. The shot count change makes the gun lose its ability to one hit kill opponents, and the ammo reduction lowers the average amount of kills to be achieved to a more reasonable number of 10, which is comparable to the tier 5 shotguns.

## MA40 Longshot tier decrease

After weighing the differences between the MA40 Longshot at REQ tier 3 and the [42] ONI Assault Rifle at tier 2, we've decided that the benefit of more consistent and faster kills at close range, but worse consistency at long range of the MA40 Longshot was not enough to warrant a tier 3 placement, so we've brought the weapon to REQ 2.

At REQ 2 the weapon can be compared to the ONI Assault Rifle, and players have a choice of either a solid close-range Assault Rifle, or an average close-range, but also potentially good medium–long-range Assault Rifle.

## Scatterbound Heatwave tier decrease

While evaluating the REQ tier 5 weapons when adjusting the [44] Broken Installation, we realized that the Scatterbound Heatwave was underperforming in its average kill potential as well as vehicle damage for a tier 5 weapon. We've decided to drop the weapon to REQ tier 4, where its infantry and vehicle killing potential is matched by other offerings such as the Sentinel Beam and Cindershot.

## Multiple weapon threat level updates

We've added some visual VFX to players who are holding certain strong weapons, that should communicate their threat levels from afar. We assigned these VFX sparingly, as we don't want the meaning of said VFX to be too confusing, as we are using the same VFX for our custom powerups.

### Threat levels

VIP:
- A threat to a maximum of 2 players.
Beta Infected:
- A threat to 4 players even in the hands of a inexperienced player.
Alpha Infected:
- A threat to a whole team even in the hands of a inexperienced player.

This pull request introduces several new tests and a GitHub Actions workflow for continuous integration. The most important changes include the addition of unit tests for various utility functions, API interactions, and state management, as well as the setup of a CI pipeline.

### Continuous Integration Setup:
* [`.github/workflows/test.yml`](diffhunk://#diff-faff1af3d8ff408964a57b2e475f69a6b7c7b71c9978cccc8f471798caac2c88R1-R29): Added a GitHub Actions workflow to automate the build and test process for the project. This workflow runs on `ubuntu-latest` and includes steps for checking out the code, setting up Flutter, installing dependencies, running code analysis, and executing unit tests.

### Dependency Updates:
* [`pubspec.yaml`](diffhunk://#diff-8b7e9df87668ffa6a04b32e1769a33434999e54ae081c52e5d943c541d4c0d25R32-R38): Added `bloc_test` and `mockito` to the `dev_dependencies` section to support the new unit tests.

### Unit Tests for Utility Functions:
* [`test/core/utils/json_converters_test.dart`](diffhunk://#diff-92af05efdebcc989157b232522e5f22e3b377e3044750bd01a1da9dc39c33768R1-R31): Added unit tests for `JsonConverters` to validate the conversion of ISO8601 strings to `DateTime` objects and vice versa.
* [`test/core/utils/number_formatter_test.dart`](diffhunk://#diff-1ad25cd3a888650c22ceea6ed1413030281aed99148a5da9f91b4e48e8dc3e85R1-R19): Added unit tests for `NumberFormatter` to verify the correct formatting of numbers, especially for values less than 1000 and those 1000 and above.

### Unit Tests for API Interactions:
* [`test/pages/home/api/search_repo_api_test.dart`](diffhunk://#diff-b300825cc963b67f9cfe941aab99e6dd595f6d8551783d1d645b0f8a7a0f140eR1-R78): Added tests for `SearchRepoApiImpl` to ensure it correctly handles successful and unsuccessful API calls when searching for repositories.

### Unit Tests for State Management:
* [`test/pages/home/cubit/search_repo_cubit_test.dart`](diffhunk://#diff-b8516732d8fbce606d55c28dcb1d093bd428c0e6b058c7936984f5d636be0ef8R1-R81): Added tests for `SearchRepoCubit` to verify state transitions during repository searches, including handling of loading, success, error, and clear actions.

These changes enhance the project's robustness by ensuring critical functionalities are properly tested and that the CI pipeline automatically verifies the integrity of the codebase with every change.

A new event listener has been added to prevent gate blocks from burning.

Tested on the server to confirm that gate blocks no longer break when set on fire.

author: alexmaras
body:
This PR aims to replace `node-konfig` as a configuration management system.
Using the std library `toml` parser and `zod`, we can skip the `default.toml` altogether and add only the necessary overrides in `local.toml`, i.e.:

```toml
[server]
ports = 4000

[jobs.youtube_session]
po_token_enabled = true
frequency = "*/20 * * * *"

[networking.fetch]
timeout_ms = 10000

[networking.fetch.retry]
enabled = true
```

Zod is doing a few things here:
1. validating the incoming `local.toml` for correctness
1. handling all Typescript typing
1. defaulting values (replacing `default.toml` in this respect)
1. outputting errors when things are incorrect

The outcome of this is:
1. native TS types on a simple object - no `get()` function calls, no forcing types with `as`
2. code editor completion of config options
3. typos in config files are flagged so users can correct them
4. slightly shorter code everywhere
5. local.toml is able to have partial blocks defined (as in example above)



I'm open to changes here. Zod is pretty well regarded in schema checking, and it does the typing stuff really nicely.
The actual code to load the config is pretty small now - most of the `config.ts` file is just the zod schema definition.


NOTE:
This PR also fixes an issue where the `youtube_session.cookies` value was at the top-level in the `toml` but used as `job.youtube_session.cookies`. Looking at the code, it seems like it should be `youtube_session.cookies` from the top-level, so I've done that

This PR also changes the structure of the `networking.fetch` block as suggested previously, it's now:
```toml
[networking.fetch]
timeout_ms = 1000

[networking.fetch.retry]
enabled = true
times = 3
```

Example error when a TOML item has a typo:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84e63549-a7ff-4b73-b1f8-8f84d39422d7)

----

Close #15

author: jumpingkeycaps
body:
Cette PR contient une série d'améliorations et d'optimisations apportées à l'interface utilisateur de l'application, ainsi que des refactorisations pour améliorer la réactivité, la performance et la maintenabilité du code.

Voici les principales modifications :

- Refonte de l'UI : La structure des écrans a été retravaillée, notamment la navigation, pour offrir une expérience plus fluide et cohérente.

- Déconnexion de l'utilisateur : J'ai ajouté une fonctionnalité permettant à l'utilisateur de se déconnecter de l'application facilement.

- Suppression de médicaments : Les utilisateurs peuvent désormais supprimer un médicament de la base de données.

- Affichage de l'historique des stocks : L'historique des stocks est désormais affiché dans une bottom modal sheet avec des informations améliorées pour chaque entrée.

- Optimisation de la gestion des stocks : La gestion des stocks (ajout/suppression d'éléments) a été améliorée avec l'intégration d'un debouncer et d'un accumulateur, afin de limiter les mises à jour en base de données.

- Refactorisation du code : J'ai simplifié et refactorisé le code pour limiter la duplication et améliorer la réutilisabilité des composants UI.
 
- Amélioration de l'écran de détails des produits : Plus d'informations pertinentes sont désormais affichées pour chaque produit dans l'écran de détails.

- Optimisation des performances d'affichage : En utilisant LazyColumn et des key pour les éléments, j'ai optimisé les listes et réduit le nombre de recharges inutiles. Les flows ont été exploités pour garder une interface réactive et performante.

Cette PR apporte donc des améliorations notables en termes de réactivité, d'ergonomie et de performances globales de l'application.

Elle inclus les taches lier au ticket suivant :

- RA-30 : Ajouter le système de déconnexion des utilisateurs de Firebase Authentication
- RA-18 : Ajouter la fonctionnalité de suppression d’un médicament du stock
- RA-21 : Améliorer l'affichage esthétique de l’historique et l'intégrer dans la fiche détail d’un medicament
- RA-20 : Afficher des informations complètes dans l’historique des changements
- RA-2 : Refactorisation du code pour éviter la duplication du code
- RA-9 : Mettre en place le lazy loading pour un chargement progressif des données
- RA-81 : Implementer la barre de recherche et les boutons de trie des medicaments.

author: paavohuhtala
body:
- Fix `WndParser` crashing with ZH Steam version's `MainMenu.wnd`
  - The Steam version of base Generals doesn't have the same issue - looks like the Wnd file was modified by hand, and the ZH version has a small syntax issue which the game seems to handle without issues, but OpenSAGE didn't like it.
- Change .big file handling to override existing entries in case of duplicate filename
  - This is potentially a pretty big change, but it seems to match the original engine. I don't think `Patch` .big files could work any other way.
  - Without this change the actual load order was kind of inverted (vs how it is other games) - the files that were loaded first won, and there was no way to override their entries afterwards.
- Update .big file load order logic to match ZH Steam version
  - This is explained in comments in (hopefully) great detail 
- Support loading universal / language independent .str files
  - There is just one file like this (`Patch.str` from the current Steam version) from what I can tell.
- Load Generals / ZH Steam version's Patch.str if available
  - Required to display the `Custom Mission`  button properly in the single player menu

With these changes (with help from #1308), OpenSAGE can now boot into the shellmap in Zero Hour with the latest Steam build of the game.

author: worm-girl
body:
#### Summary
Fix major grappling bug, minor throwing bugs

#### Purpose of change
- Grappling had a major bug where if you killed an enemy while grabbing them, the game could crash.
- Throwing was not appropriately damaging enemies when they collided with obstacles.
- The throwing sidebar wasn't giving any feedback.

#### Describe the solution
- Add some proper grab cleanup code to monster::die() which ensures a grabbed monster who dies doesn't trip a segfault somewhere else.
- Change the impact() check to exempt for monsters who are actually flying, not ones who are merely airborne (lol)
- Copy the item-throwing code's sidebar stuff over to monster-throwing. This allows it to show the expected # of moves, however it shows an accuracy bar which is not correct. That's another issue.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
- The accuracy bar should instead be a throwforce bar, indicating whether the target is going to take any damage (and how much) relative to how hard you could possibly throw them.

#### Testing
Grabbed and threw guys and beat them up and it all worked.

author: nwalters512
body:
Any submissions but the three most recent aren't rendered until they're actually viewed. However, the routes that handled rendering those submissions previously weren't aware of if the panel was being rendered in the context of manual grading. This PR resolves that by propagating a value for `manualGradingInterface` into `renderPanelsForSubmission`.

When we force the instructor question preview to show the manual grading interface as implemented in #11528, we need to propagate the fact that we've been forced into that state back into the route that serves the submission HTML. This PR adds such a parameter to `QuestionContainer` and drills it down to `SubmissionPanel`.

This pull request includes changes to the `Search` class in the `packages/search/src/core.ts` file to handle binary file extensions more effectively. Enhancements to binary file handling:

author: ipaulobahia
body:
Este Pull Request implementa um sistema completo de agendamentos com autenticação JWT, integração com serviços e configuração de ambiente. A implementação segue uma arquitetura modular e utiliza práticas recomendadas do NestJS.

### Principais alterações:

1. **Configuração e infraestrutura base:**
   - Implementação da validação de configurações de ambiente
   - Integração com o Prisma para acesso ao banco de dados
   - Configuração do Swagger para documentação da API
   - Remoção de componentes desnecessários (testes iniciais, AppService)

2. **Módulo de Agendamentos:**
   - Criação de modelo de negócio para agendamentos
   - Implementação de DTOs para criação e cancelamento de agendamentos
   - Desenvolvimento de repositório e interface para manipulação de dados
   - Validação de entidades antes da execução de operações
   - Implementação de rotas para gerenciamento completo de agendamentos

3. **Autenticação e Segurança:**
   - Implementação de autenticação JWT com estratégia personalizada
   - Criação de decoradores para rotas públicas e obtenção de ID do negócio
   - Validação de expiração de tokens
   - Configuração de cabeçalhos e payload JWT

4. **Integração de Serviços:**
   - Implementação do módulo de serviços com controlador e repositório
   - Integração dos serviços com o módulo de agendamentos
   - Validação da existência do estabelecimento antes de operações de serviço

5. **Melhorias Estruturais:**
   - Criação do SharedRepositoryModule para exportação centralizada de repositórios
   - Ordenação melhorada das operações na documentação Swagger
   - Utilização de injeção de dependências para melhor manutenibilidade

Esta implementação fornece uma base sólida para o sistema de agendamentos, com foco em segurança, modularidade e facilidade de manutenção.

author: iksnae
body:
This PR addresses two specific issues with the PDF output format:

## Issues Fixed

1. **Separate TOC Page Numbers**: The Table of Contents now uses Roman numerals (i, ii, iii), while the main content uses Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3). This provides a clear separation between frontmatter and main content.

2. **First Content Page Starts on New Page After TOC**: Added an explicit page break and page counter reset after the Table of Contents to ensure the first chapter always starts on a fresh page.

## Implementation Details

The changes include:

1. Modified the LaTeX template to:
   - Use `\pagenumbering{roman}` for frontmatter (title page, TOC)
   - Add `\clearpage` after the Table of Contents 
   - Reset page numbering with `\pagenumbering{arabic}` for main content
   - Reset page counter with `\setcounter{page}{1}` when main content begins

2. Added an explicit `\newpage` directive before the first chapter content in the generated markdown.

3. Enhanced the "plain" page style to improve the appearance of special pages like the title page and chapter beginnings.

These changes follow standard book formatting conventions where frontmatter (title page, TOC, etc.) uses Roman numerals, and the main content starts with page 1 in Arabic numerals.

## Testing

This has been tested to ensure:
- The title page and TOC use Roman numerals
- The main content starts with page 1
- There is a clean page break between the TOC and first chapter

The changes maintain all the previous improvements to the build process while adding these specific formatting enhancements.

author: jadonylin
body:
Since we are moving from the LvR optimisation results (and the botched MdS softmin results), it will be easier to work with the twobox that has working, updating self.params, rather than switching between branches to analyse results from different FOMs. 

In the new, merged jl, if you want to extract the results from the LvR and MdS-softmin optimisation for plotting or calculations, you will need to manually recreate the twobox gratings using the twobox syntax. This is achieved by inserting the appropriate parameters (saved in the curated-optimum .txt files) into TwoBox. Do not use extract_opt or extract the twobox objects from the .pkl files directly, or else the optima's parameters (which were previously saved in twobox.params) will be overwritten by the new (correct) logic for creating and updating twobox.params. That is, in jl-selfparams-outdated, the optimised gratings were saved as twobox objects, and the optimum parameters were saved in twobox.params. However, since the twobox.params logic was incorrect in jl-selfparams-outdated, the optimum parameters were **only** saved in twobox.params, not in the individual instance variables. Hence, in jl-selfparams-outdated, the instance variables such as twobox.grating_pitch and twobox.box1eps are still equal to their default, initial values (given to the optimiser). If you attempt to extract these optimised twobox objects from the .pkl files in the jl branch, the optimised parameters in twobox.params will be overwritten by those default, initial values because twobox.params is initialised by the individual instance variables upon creation of the twobox. 

This is not an issue for gratings that were optimised using the jl branch's twobox class, for which the optimised parameters were correctly stored in both the individual instance variables and the twobox.params instance variable.

author: dkweiss31
body:
Follow up on https://github.com/dynamiqs/dynamiqs/pull/748, reimplementing the smart sampling algorithm whereby the no-jump trajectory is only sampled once. I want to offer my thanks again to @gautierronan for your heroic simplification of my initial overcomplicated implementation, which I'm only now internalizing upon diving into this reimplementation. A few notes/questions

1. In this implementation, the trajectories are the final (rightmost) batch dimension (this is actually consistent with the previous version of the API docstring) as opposed to previously where they were the leftmost. I like them being leftmost, because it is natural to sum/average over `axis=0`. However this would require some inelegant `moveaxis` calls at the end of `_vectorized_jssesolve`. Thoughts?
2. To keep things simple, the no-jump and jump results are returned together, with e.g. `result.states[..., 0, :, :]` containing the no-click trajectory and `result.states[..., 1:, :, :]` containing the click trajectories (similarly for expectation values). Actually calculating averaged quantities is thus a little complicated for the user. They must call e.g. (if there are no other batch dimensions)
```python
noclick_prob = jsseresult.final_state_norm[0]
mean_jsse_expects_click = jnp.mean(jsseresult.expects[1:], axis=0)
mean_jsse_expects = (
      noclick_prob_expect * jsseresult.expects[0]
      + (1 - noclick_prob_expect) * mean_jsse_expects_click
)
```
to calculate expectation values. I wonder if this is something we can implement in the result class? We'd need to worry then also about batch dimensions.

body:
Add asserts to check vertex bounds in graph methods and add corresponding tests.

* **Directed Graph:**
  - Add asserts to `add_edge`, `del_edge`, and `has_edge` methods to check if `x` and `y` are within bounds and return the index in the message.
  - Add an empty line after the last assert in `add_edge`, `del_edge`, and `has_edge` methods.

* **Undirected Graph:**
  - Add asserts to `add_edge`, `del_edge`, and `has_edge` methods to check if `x` and `y` are within bounds and return the index in the message.
  - Add an empty line after the last assert in `add_edge`, `del_edge`, and `has_edge` methods.

* **Tests:**
  - Add tests for `add_edge`, `del_edge`, and `has_edge` methods in both directed and undirected graphs to check if the correct index is returned in the assert message when out of bounds.

author: squeemishly
body:
This change started with replacing the old ascii network map with the new image network map. In the process of doing that, I needed to update all of the machine names. At that point, it meant we were starting with an internet that only had a client and a router. That don't make no sense.

I decided to make our internet start with all networks and machines fully added and ready to go. That wasn't the interesting part of the chapter anyway. This change also means that our readers won't need to do anything with docker or docker compose in this chapter, and I think we can all agree that that's a win.

author: dinamow
body:
This pull request introduces several new features and modifications to the backend of the application, specifically related to room management. The changes include adding new endpoints, modifying existing database schema, and updating the controller logic to support these new features.

Key changes include:

### New Endpoints and Controller Methods:
* Added `myRooms` endpoint to fetch all rooms created by the user. This endpoint retrieves the user's rooms and fetches detailed information for each room from an external service (`Backend/backend/controllers/Daily.controller.js`).
* Added `getRoomByName` endpoint to fetch a room by its name. This endpoint retrieves room information based on the room name provided in the request parameters (`Backend/backend/controllers/Daily.controller.js`).

### Database Schema Update:
* Modified the `UserRoom` model to replace the `roomId` field with `roomName` to better align with the new room management logic (`Backend/prisma/schema.prisma`).

### Route Definitions:
* Updated the routes to include the new `myRooms` and `getRoomByName` endpoints and added Swagger documentation for these endpoints (`Backend/backend/routes/daily.route.js`).

### Controller Logic Adjustments:
* Updated the `__createRoom` method to use `roomName` instead of `roomId` when creating a new room entry (`Backend/backend/controllers/Daily.controller.js`).

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.3** to **7.7.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

.. _issue 1888: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1888
.. _pull 1919: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1919


.. _changes_7-6-12:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.12
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing (`issue 1927`_).  These are now
  building reliably.

.. _issue 1927: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1927

.. _changes_7-6-11:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#pep-649-deferred-evaluation-of-annotations


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to

   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra
  "didn't," as described in `issue 1873`_.  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1873: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1873
.. _issue 1876: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1876


.. _changes_7-6-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.2
   ```
   --------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: a final wildcard match/case clause assigning to a name (``case _ as
  value``) was incorrectly marked as a missing branch.  This is now fixed,
  closing `issue 1860`_.

- Fewer things are considered branches now. Lambdas, comprehensions, and
  generator expressions are no longer marked as missing branches if they don't
  complete execution.  Closes `issue 1852`_.

- Fix: the HTML report didn't properly show multi-line f-strings that end with
  a backslash continuation.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 1836`_, thanks
  to `LiuYinCarl and Marco Ricci <pull 1838_>`_.

- Fix: the LCOV report now has correct line numbers (fixing `issue 1846`_) and
  better branch descriptions for BRDA records (fixing `issue 1850`_).  There
  are other changes to lcov also, including a new configuration option
  :ref:`line_checksums <config_lcov_line_checksums>` to control whether line
  checksums are included in the lcov report.  The default is false. To keep
  checksums set it to true.  All this work is thanks to Zack Weinberg
  (`pull 1849`_ and `pull 1851`_).

- Fixed the docs for multi-line regex exclusions, closing `issue 1863`_.

- Fixed a potential crash in the C tracer, closing `issue 1835`_, thanks to
  `Jan Kühle <pull 1843_>`_.

.. _issue 1835: https://github.com/nedbat/cover
